intent: Let a KCD2 dice-solver inventory move between devices — download/load a .json file, copy or paste the JSON, and share a link that carries the inventory in its URL fragment — and deploy the result at https://dice.kuhy.duckdns.org/.
scope: kcd2_dice_solver/src/lib/inventoryIo.ts — one validator plus the clipboard/save-file/url-hash ports
kcd2_dice_solver/src/App.tsx — shared-link arrival, deferred persistence, dropped-payload notices
kcd2_dice_solver/deploy_build.sh — the single build path used by both setup and the post-commit hook
linux_configuration/scripts/single_use/features/setup_kcd2_dice_solver.sh — serves dist/ behind the shared gitea-caddy edge
Non-goal: no change to the solver core, the dice/badge data, or the scoring model
changes: Moved inventory persistence out of App.tsx into src/lib/inventoryIo.ts, so localStorage, a pasted file, the clipboard and a shared link all funnel through one validator that sanitises rather than rejects (unknown ids, bad counts and duplicates are dropped and reported, not thrown away silently).

Added import/export UI: download .json, copy JSON, copy share link, load a file, and paste-to-import, with clipboard and download injected as ports because navigator.clipboard and URL.createObjectURL are absent under jsdom.
Shared links encode base64url of the JSON rather than a positional scheme, because DICE is sorted alphabetically and a die added in a later patch would silently redefine every previously-shared link.
A link-loaded inventory is NOT written to storage on arrival; persistence is deferred until the visitor presses Keep or edits anything, so a shared link cannot silently overwrite a saved loadout.

FIX (found in review, was a real defect): a damaged fragment such as #i=@@@ still parses to a non-null result holding an EMPTY inventory, so `fromLink?.inventory ?? loadInventory(store)` never fell through — the visitor's own saved dice vanished from the page with no explanation. Extracted isEmptyInventory/isUsable into inventoryIo.ts as the single definition of 'worth applying', used now by both the paste box and the link path; App.tsx applies a link only when usable and otherwise falls back to storage.

Surfaced ParseResult.dropped on the link path, which was previously computed and discarded: a partially-usable link now shows 'Ignored: Unknown die ...' and an unusable one shows 'That link carried nothing usable, so this is what is saved here.'
Added a .notice.bad style (warning accent, same shape as .notice) for the damaged/incomplete case.

deploy_build.sh builds into dist.staging/ and rsyncs into dist/, and asserts the dist/ inode is unchanged: the serving container bind-mounts dist/ at /srv, so any rm -rf + mv would silently detach the mount and serve stale files forever with no error.

verification.evidence: 15 files, 280 tests passed. Coverage 100%: statements 856/856, branches 373/373, functions 179/179, lines 804/804. Includes 2 new regression tests that fail against the pre-fix code.

verification.command: regression check — new tests fail before the fix
verification.evidence: Before the fix, 'keeps the saved inventory, and says so, when the link is damaged' failed with the rendered DOM showing '0 dice' plus the 'Loaded from a shared link' banner, proving the saved lucky:1 inventory was discarded. After the fix both new tests pass.

verification.command: pnpm exec tsc --noEmit; pnpm exec eslint src
verification.evidence: TSC=0 ESLINT=0 (exit codes asserted directly; an earlier ${PIPESTATUS[0]} check was a bash-ism under zsh and asserted nothing).
Published 4 files to dist (inode 87041124, unchanged before and after rsync, so the container bind mount is still attached).
All 13 checks OK: container running, listening only on 8089, Caddy snippet present, DNS resolves, external https OK, post-commit rebuild hook and unit installed.
HTTP 200 public and 200 on 127.0.0.1:8089; served bundle is assets/index-CjacUXQ5.js, byte-identical to the hash just built, confirming the live site serves this change and not a stale build.
No matches across all 77 dice/badge ids, so btoa() in toBase64Url cannot throw on current data.

risks: NOT verified in a real browser: headless chromium is blocked by this environment's permission layer, so the fragment round-trip was verified only in jsdom (with the real solver and real modules, not stubs) plus HTTP/bundle-hash checks against the live site. Browser-specific APIs on this path — btoa/atob, URLSearchParams, history.replaceState — are standard, but a human should open the share link once to confirm.

toBase64Url uses btoa, which throws on any character above U+00FF. All 77 current ids are ASCII and the validator only ever admits known ids, so this is unreachable today; a future die added with a non-ASCII id would white-screen the page at render, since shareUrl is computed during render.
A shared link is applied over the local inventory on arrival (by design — following a link is deliberate). It is not persisted until Keep or an edit, so a reload recovers the saved loadout.

The inner Caddyfile needs auto_https off and an explicit http:// scheme: a bare 127.0.0.1:8089 address reads as a hostname, so Caddy would serve TLS on 8089 and start an HTTP->HTTPS redirect listener on :80 that, under host networking, would contend with the shared edge and could break ACME for every domain on this host. This is encoded in setup_kcd2_dice_solver.sh, not only in the generated file.
rollback: git revert the commit, then run kcd2_dice_solver/deploy_build.sh to republish the previous bundle into the existing dist/ inode.
Validate: setup_kcd2_dice_solver.sh status reports all checks OK, and curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://dice.kuhy.duckdns.org/ returns 200.
Saved inventories survive a rollback: STORAGE_KEY is unchanged and the older loadInventory tolerates the same JSON shape.
